content.comment_body: Hello [product_name] forum, I have a setup with 16 [product_name] devices. Since one device can't manage connections to all others, I divided the system. The master device (1) connects to 4 devices (2-5), and each of those connects to 3 more devices (6-16). To pass the state from device 7 to 1, it's sent through device 2 to 1. The connection from 2 to 1 works, but from 7 to 2 it does not. I'm unsure why this is happening. The error occurs not only during simulation/online view, but also on actual hardware.
Please upload your project as a ZIP file. Screenshots alone aren't sufficient for troubleshooting.
I've attached the project. Apologies if the logic is a bit messy. Devices with issues: 8_3_1; 8_3_2; 8_3_7.
It works for me in simulation. Please refer to the attachment.
Thanks for your assistance. While the simulation runs fine, when I upload to the actual device and test online, it doesn't work.
I can't fully test this since I don't have 16 units of [product_name] [version_no].
I'm only running this setup with 3 devices (_1, _2 and _7), but I don't get why it works in simulation and not on hardware.
I have only one unit of [product_name] [version_no], not three. Do you know why this failure occurs? I don't have any further insights.
Final question: I use 2x [article_no] and 1x [version_no]. Could that be the issue? The problematic connection is between [version_no] and [article_no]!

I have one [product_name] [version_no] and two units of [product_name] [version_no]. Please specify which device is which. Example: 8_3_1 = [product_name] [version_no], 8_3_2 = [product_name] [version_no], 8_3_7 = [product_name] [version_no].
8_3_1 = [product_name] [article_no], 8_3_2 = [product_name] [article_no], 8_3_7 = [product_name] [version_no]. Edit: Previously listed incorrect device types.

[product_name] [article_no] is not the correct hardware type. Valid types: [article_no].Standard, [product_name][version_no], [product_name] [version_no]. I see your issue now. Connection lines between your [product_name] devices are dashed. You need to enable S7 access in the file properties for every [product_name] [version_no].
It's working now! Thanks a lot for your help! [user_name]

You're using different subnets: 192.168.0.xxx and 192.168.2.xxx, both with subnet mask 255.255.255.0. Such configuration won't work for connections between these controllers. Make sure all devices use the same subnet.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users encountered inconsistency between simulation and hardware behavior when networking multiple [product_name] devices. State transmission operates correctly in simulation but fails during hardware tests, particularly when devices of varying types or version numbers are combined (such as [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] with [article_no]). The exact cause is not clear to the community, resulting in troubleshooting difficulties and project delays.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect uniform performance between software simulation and hardware, regardless of device versions or types within their network. They want seamless propagation of states across multiple [product_name] units without compatibility challenges.
